entities.name: Trans-Saharan Trade
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: A network of trade routes crossing the Sahara Desert (c. 300 CE – 16th century at peak) that exchanged West African gold, ivory, and slaves for North African salt, textiles, and manufactured goods. The trade created the great empires of Ghana, Mali, and Songhai, made Timbuktu a center of learning, and linked sub-Saharan Africa to the Mediterranean world.
